transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

I’ve been feeling like I’ve ruined things for everyone. I fell behind at work, and I lost control of the apartment situation, and I just can’t shake the feeling that it’s all my fault—that I deserve whatever bad thing happens next.
Can you tell me when these feelings first started and whether they began around a particular event or change in your life?
It started about a year and two months ago. The pipe burst, and I had to move into a smaller apartment. After that, my routines kind of fell apart, and the feelings have been there ever since.
Over the past year, would you say you've felt down or lost interest in things nearly every day, for most of the day?
Yeah, most days. I wake up with this flat, heavy sadness, and things I used to enjoy—putting on a record, cooking, messing with electronics—they just don’t do much for me anymore.

Before this past year, had you ever gone through a separate period—lasting at least a couple of weeks—where you felt this same kind of deep depression, or is this the first time you've experienced something like this?
I’m not really sure. I can’t think of another separate time like this before the past year.

Over this past year, has the severity of your depression stayed pretty steady and low-grade the whole time, or have there been certain stretches where it got much worse and more intense than at other times?
I’m not sure I can really separate it into worse stretches. It’s mostly just felt like this ongoing heaviness since it started.

During this past year, has your depression been severe enough to significantly disrupt your sleep, appetite, concentration, or ability to function at work and home, or has it felt more like a low-grade, manageable sadness that you've been able to push through most days?

I’m still working, but it’s been harder. I had to ask for accommodations and for people to review my documentation more, because I’m making mistakes I normally wouldn’t. At home, I skip some board-game nights and don’t leave the apartment as much. Keeping up with regular routines just takes more out of me than it used to.
Over this past year, have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or weight—either eating much more or much less than usual, or losing or gaining weight without trying?
I haven’t really noticed any major change in my appetite or weight.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep over this past year—trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping much more than usual?
Yeah. I’ll lie awake for hours listening for noises in the apartment. Then when I finally do fall asleep, I’m up before dawn, already tense and exhausted—like I never really shut down.
Over this past year, have you had any thoughts of death, dying, or that you might be better off not being here?
I don’t have a plan to hurt myself. But sometimes I think it would be easier if I just didn’t wake up, and nobody had to deal with me anymore.

Over this past year, has there been any stretch of two months or longer where you felt back to your normal self, without the sadness or loss of interest, or has it really been continuous the whole time?

No, I haven’t really had a stretch where I felt normal again. It’s been pretty continuous—about a year and two months now, since the pipe burst and I had to move into this smaller apartment and my routines kind of fell apart.

Overall, would you say you're still able to push through and manage most of your daily activities despite the difficulty, or has it become nearly impossible for you to carry out almost any of your usual activities?

I’m still working, so it’s not like I can’t do anything. But I’ve had to ask for accommodations and for people to review my work more, because I’m making documentation mistakes I normally wouldn’t. And I skip some board-game nights, leave the apartment less... keeping up with regular routines just takes more out of me now.

Would you say that, even with the accommodations, you're still able to carry out your work tasks on your own, or has it reached a point where you feel unable to function at work without significant help from others?

I can still do the work myself. I just need the accommodations and someone to look over things more often because I’m catching less of my own documentation mistakes. It’s harder than it used to be, but I’m still functioning at work.
